text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

Cricketer CHARLES BANNERMAN, who scored Australia's first test century, was born in England in 1851. BANNERMAN was also the first player to score a five, for hitting the ball over the fence, but not on the full.

Dame ALICE CHISHOLM was born in 1856. During World War I she wanted to be near her wounded son, so she set up her "Mother Chisholm's Soldiers' Canteens" in Egypt. She provided the desert troops with fresh bread and showers, and cooked up to 60,000 eggs a day.

West Indian boxer PETER JACKSON was born in 1861. He was trained in Australia by LARRY FOLEY and became Australian champion. JACKSON went to the United States but because he was black he wasn't allowed to fight for the world title. JACKSON's tomb at Toowong cemetery in Brisbane bears the inscription "This was a man".
American actor, dancer and writer GEORGE M. COHAN was born in 1878. He gave the world "Yankee Doodle Dandy", "Over There" and "Give My Regards to Broadway".
Czech-born playwright TOM STOPPARD, who wrote "Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are Dead", was born in 1937.
Singer/songwriter PAUL ANKA was born in 1941.

Australian singer JUDITH DURHAM, who was the first female lead singer with the 'Seekers', was born in 1943 in Melbourne. JUDITH joined the group after their falsetto male lead left. Their hits included "I'll never find another you" (1965), "A World of our own" (1965), "The Carnival is Over" (1965) and "Morningtown Ride" and "Georgy Girl" both in 1966. She left the Seekers in 1967 and returned to sing with them again in 1994.
British guitarist, keyboard player and singer with the group Babys, MIKE CORBY, was born in 1955.
Australian bass player and singer with Icehouse, STEPHEN MORGAN, was born in 1960.
** EVENTS **
1863 : A turning point occurred in the American Civil War
with the defeat of the Confederate's General ROBERT E. LEE'S forces at Gettysburg. General LEE lost more than a third of his force of 70,000 men during the three day battle.
1928 : The first television set went on sale with a price
tag of 75 dollars.
1954 : The rations system came to end in Britain, as
post-war shortages finished.
1958 : A report was released in Melbourne that a new
international airport was to be built at Tullamarine on the city outskirts.
1898 : Captain JOSHUA SLOCUM arrived at Newport, Rhode
Island, after completing the first solo circumnavigation of the world.
1905 : In Odessa, Russian troops killed more than 6,000
people to restore order during a strike.
1928 : JOHN LOGIE BAIRD transmitted the world's first
colour television transmission in London.
1960 : Australia's JACK BRABHAM won the French Grand
Prix.
1965 : ROY EMERSON and MARGARET SMITH won the Wimbledon
singles titles, giving Australia the double crown in lawn tennis for the first time ever in the same year.
1970 : In Spain, a British Comet aircraft crashed,
killing all 112 on board.
1971 : Lead singer with The Doors, JIM MORRISON, died of
a heart attack in Paris.
1976 : Twenty-year old BJORN BORG became the youngest
ever men's singles winner at Wimbledon. The Swede showed early promise at tennis, winning his first tournament at the age of eleven.
1987 : The "Butcher of Lyons", KLAUS BARBIE, was

convicted of crimes against humanity. The NAZI SS commander in Lyons during World War II was responsible for tracking down resistance workers and Jews, including rounding-up Jewish children. He was also notorious for torturing resistance leader JEAN MOULIN. BARBIE escaped capture at the ?nd of the war and was employed by US intelligence in Germany, until moving to Bolivia in 1951. The Bolivian authorities turned him over to the French in 1983.
1988 : American warship Vincennes shot down an Iran
Airbus A300 over the Gulf in the last weeks of the Iran-Iraq war, killing all 290 aboard.
1990 : The hero of the Chernobyl nuclear accident died of

leukemia in an American hospital. ANATOLI GRISHCHENKO braved radioactive fallout to fly a helicopter over the crippled power station, to dump loads of sand and concrete to seal the plant and prevent a meltdown. The nuclear power plant disaster occured in April 1986, when fire broke out at the reactor, causing the world's worst ever nuclear accident to date.
1996 : Russian President BORIS YELTSIN won the runoff
vote against Communist leader GENNADY ZYUGANOV to retain the presidency.
1996 : British Prime Minister JOHN MAJOR announces that
the historic Stone of Scone, the ancient symbol of Scottish kings, is to be removed from London's Westminster Abbey after 700 years and returned to Scotland.
